• The case involved a traffic stop, a vehicle search that was justified by probable cause, and a subsequent “post‑stop” detention that lasted longer than the typical “reasonable” period.
• The Ohio Supreme Court held that the detention was **not** an unlawful seizure because it was an integral part of the search and was necessary for the officers to collect evidence and guard the scene.
• The Court cited *Terry v. Ohio* and *United States v. Mendenhall* in discussing the “reasonable” period for post‑stop detentions.
• The holding was that the detention, though prolonged, was still within the scope of the original stop and did not violate the Fourth Amendment. | | **Does the citation support the claim?** | **Yes**.
